title: LockDown Browser Student Guide
content_markdown:
[Image](https://lthub.ubc.ca/files/2020/08/LockDown-Browser-Icon-e1597346097854-299x300.png)

**LockDown Browser is a web browser that controls what you can do during a Canvas assessment\.** When your instructor has you use LockDown Browser for an assessment, you will not be able to print or copy questions, visit other websites, access other applications, including tools that create overlays or interact with your screen\. You will also not be able to close the assessment until it is submitted\. Assessments created for use with LockDown Browser cannot be taken with standard browsers\.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Access** | *Immediate* | You can access LockDown Browser from your computer as soon as you [download LockDown Browser](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/lockdown-browser-student-guide/#download)\. |
| **Bandwidth** | *Yes* | Low demand on internet connections\. |
| **Privacy** | *Yes* | Complies with UBC’s privacy requirements\. |

### What will I use it for?

Your instructor may have you use LockDown Browser for course assessments:

-   Take assessments in Canvas with restrictions intended to ensure fairness
-   Review outcomes of assessments in Canvas with restrictions intended to protect the questions and answers

This tool guide was last reviewed in March 2026\.

## What do I need to use LockDown Browser?

### A desktop or laptop computer with LockDown Browser

You will need to download the LockDown Browser web browser on a desktop or laptop computer\.

Although you can download the [LockDown Browser app](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/lockdown-browser/id659101775) on an iPad, we do not recommend using an iPad due to technical difficulties and incompatibilities that can occur\.

Chromebooks and other mobile devices do not work with LockDown Browser at UBC\. You can view the [minimum technical requirements for LockDown Browser](https://support.respondus.com/hc/en-us/articles/4409607170459-What-are-the-computer-requirements-for-installations-of-Respondus-LockDown-Browser-) on LockDown Browser’s support site\.

#### Tips

-   **You can uninstall LockDown Browser once you finish your assessment\.** Follow the [steps for uninstalling LockDown Browser](https://support.respondus.com/hc/en-us/articles/4409595418907-How-do-I-uninstall-or-remove-LockDown-Browser-) on LockDown Browser’s support site\.
-   **You can use LockDown Browser on a UBC computer instead of downloading it on your own device\.** Find details in our FAQ on [other options for taking LockDown Browser assessments](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/lockdown-browser-student-guide/#other-options) below\.
-   **Avoid virtual machines or Linux\.** LockDown Browser does not run on virtual machines or Linux\-based systems\. Use a Windows or macOS computer instead\.

## How do I use LockDown Browser?

You will first need to download LockDown Browser, then prepare to take your LockDown Browser assessment in Canvas\.

Click any accordion bar below for instructions and tips for using LockDown Browser\.

Expand All

[> Download LockDown Browser](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/lockdown-browser-student-guide/#download)

### Download LockDown Browser

If you see "Requires Respondus LockDown Browser" next to an assessment name in Canvas, you will need to download LockDown Browser\. You will not be able to take a LockDown Browser assessment in a standard browser \(e\.g\., Chrome, Firefox, Safari\)\.

1.  Go to the [LockDown Browser download page](https://www.respondus.com/lockdown/download.php?id=695714529)\.
2.  Click **Download**\.
3.  Follow the on\-screen instructions to complete the download\.

#### Tips

-   **If you have used LockDown Browser before, make sure it is updated to the latest version\.** To check and update your version, open LockDown Browser and click the info button \(the "i" button\) in the toolbar\.

[> Prepare for a LockDown Browser assessment](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/lockdown-browser-student-guide/#prepare-for-assessment)

### Prepare for a LockDown Browser assessment

-   **Ensure that LockDown Browser is ready in advance\.** Confirm that you meet the [minimum technical requirements for LockDown Browser](https://support.respondus.com/hc/en-us/articles/4409607170459-What-are-the-computer-requirements-for-installations-of-Respondus-LockDown-Browser) by downloading, installing, and opening the browser ahead of time\.
-   **Complete any LockDown Browser mock quiz, or request for one to be set up\.** This practice allows you to try out the experience before the stakes are high\. You can also enroll yourself in the [Chapman Learning Common's Exam Practice Course](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/C7TG94) and test out the LockDown Browser mock quiz that is set up there\.
-   **Know that your instructor will be able to set up access to any files, websites, or tools you might need for the exam\.** For example, you will be able to open a spreadsheet in a quiz question, click a link in a quiz question, or use a calculator tool as needed\.
-   **Avoid running AI tools or apps that use virtual environment\.** Apps that create overlays, run in sandboxes, or use virtual machine\-style environments, including some AI study tools, can cause LockDown Browser to block your exam attempt\. Respondus may treat these tools as bypass attempts, which can lead to an account ban\. [What should I do if I see a LockDown Browser ban message?](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/lockdown-browser-student-guide/#banned)

#### Tips

-   **If you need to submit an assessment in a language different from your default keyboard, you can update your keyboard settings ahead of time\.** Find details below in our FAQ on [how to set up a different language keyboard in LockDown Browser\.](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/lockdown-browser-student-guide/#keyboard)

[> Take a LockDown Browser assessment in Canvas](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/lockdown-browser-student-guide/#take-assessment)

### Take a LockDown Browser assessment in Canvas

If you see "Requires Respondus LockDown Browser" next to an assessment name in Canvas, you will need to use LockDown Browser to take that assessment\. We recommend taking any timed assessment on a desktop or laptop computer, as they are more reliable than using the iPad app\.

> Note that once in LockDown Browser, you will not be able to access these instructions; you can read them for now\.

1.  Open the LockDown Browser application\.
2.  If a prompt appears from LockDown Browser to close a blocked program \(e\.g\., screen capture, instant messaging\), choose to close the process or application\.
3.  You will automatically be directed to log in to Canvas using your UBC CWL \(Campus\-Wide Login\)\. Navigate to your Canvas course and click **Quizzes** in the Course Navigation\.
    -   You may need to complete a multi\-factor authentication on your phone or hardware token before you are logged in to Canvas\.
4.  Click the **assessment name**\.
    -   If you are unable to open the assessment through LockDown Browser, you can try to access it from a standard browser\. In your regular browser, log in to your Canvas course and re\-enter the assessment\. Click to begin, then click **Open LockDown Browser** to open the assessment in LockDown Browser\.
5.  You may be prompted to enter an "Access Code" before you can begin, which your instructor will have given to you\. After entering the access code, click **Submit**\.
6.  Click either **Take the Quiz** or **Begin** \(whichever you see\)\.
    -   You might be prompted to restart LockDown Browser\. This prompt is normal for a certain type of Canvas quiz and not a reason to be concerned\.
7.  Once you have completed the assessment, click either **Submit Quiz** or **Submit** \(whichever you see\)\.
8.  You can now close LockDown Browser\. You can also [uninstall LockDown Browser](https://support.respondus.com/hc/en-us/articles/4409595418907-How-do-I-uninstall-or-remove-LockDown-Browser-) from your device, if you would like\.

#### Tips

-   **If LockDown Browser closes your assessment unexpectedly, remain calm and notify your instructor\.** Then come back to this page to follow the troubleshooting steps in the accordion section below\.
-   **We do not recommend taking assessments on iPad, but instructions with screenshots are available\.** Follow the [steps for using LockDown Browser on iPad for different types of Canvas quizzes](https://support.respondus.com/hc/en-us/articles/4409607211163-Can-an-iPad-be-used-to-take-a-LockDown-Browser-exam-instructions-for-students-) on LockDown Browser's support site\.

[> Troubleshoot issues with a LockDown Browser assessment in Canvas](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/lockdown-browser-student-guide/#troubleshoot-issues)

### Troubleshoot issues with a LockDown Browser assessment in Canvas

When LockDown Browser closes or appears to freeze, it is commonly due to one of the following: having a pop\-up from another application appear behind LockDown Browser \(meaning it will be hidden from you\), clicking a corrupted web link \(which LockDown Browser will block\), or losing your internet connection\.

In these cases, you may get bumped out of the assessment temporarily\. Try to remain calm and walk through the steps below\.

1.  Let your instructor or TA know that you are having an issue, particularly if you are in a timed assessment\.
2.  If you are taking the assessment in a space with an in\-person invigilator, ask the invigilator to enter the "Proctor Exit Password" to close LockDown Browser for you\.
3.  If you are using an iPad, switch to a desktop or laptop computer\.
4.  If LockDown Browser has closed, open it again and attempt to re\-enter the assessment\. Find your way back to the question you were on using the question list in the sidebar of the Canvas quiz\.
5.  If re\-entering the assessment does not work, restart your device\. You can force a restart by holding down the device's power button for 5\-20 seconds or longer\.
6.  After you restart, close all programs that start up automatically\. Ideally, LockDown Browser should be the only application running on your device\.
7.  Disconnect any additional screens or displays connected to your device\.
8.  Temporarily disable any extra spyware detection or anti\-virus software you have added to the device\.
9.  Ensure that LockDown Browser is updated to the latest version\. To check and update your version, open LockDown Browser and click the **info button** \(the "i" button\)\.
10.  If you are at home, reset your internet connection or, if you are in a public space, forget and re\-join the network\. Then turn your internet connection off and on\.
     -   For a full reset, you can also optionally [uninstall LockDown Browser](https://support.respondus.com/hc/en-us/articles/4409595418907-How-do-I-uninstall-or-remove-LockDown-Browser-) and download it again using the instructions in the earlier accordion section of this guide\.
11.  Open LockDown Browser and attempt to re\-enter the assessment again\. Find your way back to the question you were on using the question list in the sidebar of the Canvas quiz\.
12.  If you still have issues, contact the help desk below\.

## LockDown Browser FAQ

Find UBC\-specific answers to frequently asked questions by clicking any accordion bar below\.

[> How can I practice using LockDown Browser before an assessment?](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/lockdown-browser-student-guide/#practice)

You can test LockDown Browser before an exam by taking a mock quiz that may be set up by your instructor in Canvas\. Taking a LockDown Browser mock quiz will give you a sense of what using LockDown Browser is like and help confirm that your device is compatible and nothing installed creates conflicts\.

Testing in advance is strongly recommended, even if you have used LockDown Browser before\. A practice attempt can help identify software or system conflicts early, when there is time to address them\. This reduces the chance of unexpected issues that could prevent you from starting an exam\.

If your instructor has not set up a mock quiz in your course, you can ask if one could be set up\. You can also [enrol in the Chapman Learning Common's Exam Practice Course](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/C7TG94) on Canvas and take the mock quiz that is set up there\. Once you are enrolled in the course, click **Quizzes** in the Course Navigation and select the **Lockdown Browser Exam \- Requires Respondus LockDown Browser** mock quiz\.

[> What should I do if I see a LockDown Browser ban message?](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/lockdown-browser-student-guide/#student-account-ban)

If LockDown Browser shows a message saying your account has been banned, do not panic\. This does not mean you have done something wrong\. It simply means the system detected software or activity that could interfere with LockDown Browser and has temporarily blocked access as a precaution\.

A ban is a technical flag, not an academic misconduct decision\.

In some cases, issues like this can be avoided by testing LockDown Browser in advance using a practice or mock quiz\. Testing early helps identify potential software conflicts before exam day, when there is time to resolve them\.

Bans are uncommon and are used as a last\-resort security measure\. When a ban is in place, you will not be able to start exams that require LockDown Browser, even in other courses, until the issue is reviewed\.

If you see a ban message:

1.  Write down the reference code shown in the message\. This code is required to investigate what happened\.
2.  Contact your instructor as soon as possible and share the reference code with them\.
3.  Your instructor will connect with the LT Hub to review the situation\.
4.  The LT Hub will work with Respondus Support to have the ban removed\.

A LockDown Browser ban is linked to your user account, not your computer\. Reinstalling LockDown Browser, switching devices, or changing networks will not resolve the issue\.

The important thing to know is that support is available, and most situations can be reviewed and resolved once the reference code is shared\.

[> Can I use a device other than my own to take an assessment with LockDown Browser?](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/lockdown-browser-student-guide/#other-options)

Yes\. If your device does not meet the minimum technical requirements, or if it has software or system settings that may interfere with LockDown Browser, we recommend borrowing a UBC desktop or laptop computer\. At UBC Vancouver, you can [borrow a laptop from the Irving K\. Barber Learning Centre](https://services.library.ubc.ca/computers-technology/technology-borrowing/) or [use a desktop computer in the Chapman Learning Commons](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/use-our-computers/)\.

At UBC Okanagan, please consult the list of [UBCO Computer Labs \- Hardware and Software](https://it.ok.ubc.ca/services/computers-printers/labs/lab-details/) to find where Respondus LockDown Browser is installed\. UBCO computer labs are available for student use when not previously booked by a class\.

[> How can I use a different language keyboard in LockDown Browser?](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/lockdown-browser-student-guide/#keyboard)

Follow LockDown Browser's instructions to update keyboard language [on Windows](https://support.respondus.com/hc/en-us/articles/4409607381275-Windows-How-to-Setup-Keyboard-Language-Switching-for-LockDown-Browser) or [on mac\.](https://support.respondus.com/hc/en-us/articles/4409595702811-Mac-How-to-Setup-Keyboard-Language-Switching-for-LockDown-Browser) After adding the new keyboard to your device, you can review the tips below for additional recommendations\.

-   Avoid using the ALT key as it may trigger warnings in LockDown Browser\. To prevent this, change your language‑switching hotkey to **CTRL \+ SHIFT** or another combination that does not use the **ALT** key\.
-   Since the taskbar is hidden in LockDown Browser, you will need another way to confirm your current input language\. You can display the language pop\-up menu by holding your language\-switching keys\.
    -   For Windows, the floating language bar that you set up following the instructions from LockDown Browser may not appear for certain languages\. Instead, if your shortcut is **CTRL \+ SHIFT**, press and hold **CTRL** and tap **SHIFT** repeatedly\. A pop\-up menu will appear showing your available languages\.
    -   For Mac, when you switch between languages, your computer device will automatically display a small window showing the current input language\.
-   If you are switching to the Japanese keyboard, the default alphabet is Romaji\. As you are typing with the keyboard, you can see a list of suggested words to choose from\. You can also use the following shortcuts to manually change alphabets:
    -   Tap **CTRL \+ CAPSLOCK** to switch to Hiragana
    -   Tap **CTRL \+ SHIFT** to switch to Romaji
    -   To type in Katakana:
        1.  First switch to the Hiragana alphabet
        2.  Type out your word without pressing **Enter**
        3.  Press **F7** to convert it to Katakana\. If you would like to convert the Katakana back to Hiragana, press **F6**
        4.  Please note that if your **Fn** Lock is off, you can complete the conversion by pressing **Fn \+ F6** or **F7** accordingly\. You can also toggle on/off the **Fn** lock by pressing **Fn \+ Esc**\.

## Where can I get more support with LockDown Browser?

### Technical support

**If you have trouble with Canvas or LockDown Browser:**

-   Contact the UBC [IT Service Centre Help Desk](https://it.ubc.ca/got-question-about-it-products-and-support#helpdesk):  
    604 822 2008 or fill out the [UBC IT request form](https://ubc.service-now.com/selfservice?id=sc_cat_item_v2&sys_id=cc7f5fb9874e0100bbee70406d434df9)\.

**If you have technical issues while taking a LockDown Browser timed assessment:**

-   Let your instructor or teaching assistant know right away\.

---

### Online learning support

-   Visit UBC’s [Keep Learning site](http://keeplearning.ubc.ca/) and the Chapman Learning Common’s [student toolkits](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/category/type/interactive/)\.
-   Visit the [UBC Vancouver’s Centre for Accessibility page](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility) or the [UBC Okanagan’s Disability Resource Centre page](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/academic-success/disability-resources/) to learn more about available support for students with disabilities and ongoing medical conditions\.

#### Learn more

-   Read the [Student Support FAQ](https://support.respondus.com/hc/en-us/sections/4409607115931-Student-Support) available on LockDown Browser’s support site\.

title: LOCR Student Guide
content_markdown:
[Image](https://lthub.ubc.ca/files/2020/07/UBC-Library-Logo-150x150.jpg)

**Library Online Course Reserves \(LOCR\) is where you can access certain required readings and other content items for courses called course reserves**\. Instructors make these course reserves available for you through the UBC Library\.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Access** | *Immediate* | You can access LOCR through Canvas if your instructor has set this up, or you can [log in to LOCR](https://courses.library.ubc.ca/) outside of Canvas\. |
| **Bandwidth** | *Yes* | Low demand on internet connections\. |
| **Privacy** | *Yes* | Complies with UBC’s privacy requirements\. |

### What will I use it for?

Your instructor may ask you to use LOCR to access library items specific to the course:

-   Read electronic or physical articles and books
-   View web and media resources
-   Access PDFs of book chapters

This tool guide was last reviewed in April 2025\.

## What do I need to use LOCR?

### A supported web browser

LOCR runs in your web browser and supports the latest versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari\.

---

### A UBC course that uses course reserves

You will only see a list of items in LOCR for a course if your instructor has requested them\.

#### Tips

-   **If you recently registered for a course that uses LOCR, it may take up to 48 hours to gain access to LOCR**\. If you still have trouble accessing your course reserves after several days, please contact your instructor\.

## How do I use LOCR?

Click any accordion bar below for instructions and tips for using LOCR\.

Expand All

[> Access your course reserves in LOCR](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/locr-student-guide/#access-course-reserves)

### Access your course reserves in LOCR

There are two ways you can access course reserves in LOCR: from inside a Canvas course \(if your instructor has enabled this\) or from the standalone LOCR site\.

Please note that your course reserves might not yet appear in LOCR if they are still awaiting approval by the UBC Library\. You can speak with your instructor to confirm which resources you should currently have access to in LOCR\.

-   [From a Canvas course](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/locr-student-guide/#FromaCanvascourse-225)
-   [From the LOCR site](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/locr-student-guide/#FromtheLOCRsite-226)

1.  Log in to your Canvas course and click **Library Online Course Reserves** in the Course Navigation\.
2.  The LOCR site will open in a new tab, and you will see a list of the available course reserves\.

#### Tips

-   **Not all instructors will add LOCR to the Course Navigation in Canvas**\. If you cannot find LOCR in the Course Navigation, check if your instructor has published links to course reserves in the course modules instead\. You can also log in directly to the [standalone LOCR site](https://courses.library.ubc.ca/)\.

1.  Log in to the [standalone LOCR site](https://courses.library.ubc.ca/login.form) using your UBC CWL \(Campus\-Wide Login\)\.
2.  Select the **course** in the "Course" column\.
3.  You will see a list of the available course reserves\.

#### Tips

-   **You can filter your list of courses in LOCR**\. Check the "Show current and future courses only" and/or "Show courses with readings only" boxes\. The "Show current and future courses only" filter is turned on by default\. You can also turn off these filters to access course reserves from past courses, if they are still available\.

[> Interact with your course reserves in LOCR](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/locr-student-guide/#interact-with-course-reserves)

### Interact with your course reserves in LOCR

In LOCR, you can click any course to see its course reserves list\. Use the search box to search for a specific course reserve item by title, author, or tag\. Instructors may use tags to describe and organize the course reserves\. For example, an instructor might add a "Week 1" tag to all items that should be read in the first week of the course\.

Under the "Read" column, each item in the course reserves list will indicate if you have previously accessed it\. Clicking any item title will allow you to view an electronic item directly or see where a physical item is available on campus\.

Each electronic item has a set start and end date that indicates its availability to you in LOCR\. These availability dates mean that you may not be able to access all the course reserves after the course ends, so please download any electronic items you want to continue accessing\.

## Where can I get more support with LOCR?

### Technical support

**If you have trouble with LOCR:**

-   Contact your instructor or teaching assistant as your first point of contact\.
-   If you are having trouble accessing LOCR from Canvas, please log in to the [standalone LOCR site](https://courses.library.ubc.ca/) to access your course reserves\.
-   If you encounter errors when accessing an electronic item, contact Koerner Library at [koerner\.reserve@ubc\.ca](mailto:koerner.reserve@ubc.ca)\.
-   Contact us at the LT Hub for further assistance:  
    604 827 4775 or [LT\.hub@ubc\.ca](mailto:LT.hub@ubc.ca) or visit the [LT Hub online](https://lthub.ubc.ca/dropin)\.

---

### Online learning support

-   Visit UBC’s [Keep Learning site](http://keeplearning.ubc.ca/) and the Chapman Learning Common’s [student toolkits](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/category/type/interactive/)\.
-   Visit the [UBC Vancouver’s Centre for Accessibility page](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility) or the [UBC Okanagan’s Disability Resource Centre page](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/academic-success/disability-resources/) to learn more about available support for students with disabilities and ongoing medical conditions\.

#### Learn more

-   Explore the UBC Library’s [“Student Resources” tab for LOCR](https://services.library.ubc.ca/borrowing-services/using-course-reserves/#StudentResources-1) on the Library’s course reserves page\.

---

title: peerScholar Student Guide
content_markdown:
[peerScholar Logo](https://lthub.ubc.ca/files/2017/11/peerScholar.png)

**peerScholar is a peer review tool that allows you to exchange feedback on assignments with peers in your course**\. peerScholar assignments have three phases: creating your work, assessing your peers’ work and providing feedback, and reflecting on your own work\.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Access** | *Immediate* | You can access peerScholar through Canvas\. |
| **Bandwidth** | *Yes* | Low demand on internet connections\. |
| **Privacy** | *Yes* | Complies with UBC’s privacy requirements\. |

### What will I use it for?

Your instructor may have you use peerScholar to participate in peer review:

-   Submit assignments for peers to evaluate
-   Evaluate your peers’ work and provide feedback
-   Evaluate your own work
-   Reflect on your peers’ feedback
-   Evaluate your peers’ feedback and/or revise your work

This tool guide was last reviewed in November 2024\.

## What do I need to use peerScholar?

### A supported web browser

peerScholar runs in your web browser and supports Chrome, Firefox, or Safari\. For more information on which versions work, check the [peerScholar supported browser page](http://pearsoned.ca/highered/weir_6ce/support/system-requirements.html)\.

---

### A peerScholar student account

A peerScholar account will be created for you after you open a peerScholar assignment from Canvas\. To make sure this account is created properly, please follow the steps for enrolling as outlined in the accordion section below\.

## How do I use peerScholar?

You will first access peerScholar through your Canvas course\. Then you can participate in the course activities within the peerScholar application\.

Click any accordion bar below to find instructions and tips for using peerScholar\.

Expand All

[> Enroll in your peerScholar course](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/peerscholar-student-guide/#enroll-in-course)

### Enroll in your peerScholar course

By default, a peerScholar account will be created for you when you open a peerScholar assignment from Canvas\. To make sure your account is created properly, please follow the steps for enrolling in a peerScholar course as outlined below\.

1.  Log in to your Canvas course and find your peerScholar assignment\.
2.  Click the **peerScholar assignment** you want to open\. If prompted, click **Load \[assignment name\] in a new window**\. To ensure the assignment opens properly, please allow pop\-up windows in your browser\.
3.  If you are able to see an overview of your assigned peerScholar activities, then you have successfully enrolled in your peerScholar course\. If you do not see this overview, contact your instructor or teaching assistants so they can check your status in the peerScholar course\.

#### Tips

-   **Although peerScholar is a separate application from Canvas, you will need to access peerScholar through Canvas for each course**\. Accessing peerScholar this way ensures you are properly registered in each peerScholar course and your grades can sync with Canvas\.
-   **Assignments in peerScholar are called "activities"**\. These terms are interchangeable\.

[> Understand the peerScholar workflow](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/peerscholar-student-guide/#understand-workflow)

### Understand the peerScholar workflow

Assessments in peerScholar are completed in three stages:

1.  **Create** \- You will submit a digital assignment\. Submissions can be written or include other mediums, like images or other multimedia\.
2.  **Assess** \- You will see your peers' work to review, mark, and provide feedback on based on a set of customized rubrics from your instructor\. You may also be required to assess your own work, if your instructor has set this up\.
3.  **Reflect** \- You will read and consider your peers' feedback on your own work\. Depending on the assignment, you may be asked to evaluate each piece of feedback and/or revise and resubmit your original work based on the feedback provided\.

To learn more about the purposes and impacts of peerScholar's phases, you can read the [peerScholar vision document](https://cogneeto.s3.amazonaws.com/docs/vision/GrawemeyerLong.pdf)\.

[> Submit work with peerScholar](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/peerscholar-student-guide/#submit-work)

### Submit work with peerScholar

To access peerScholar, you will first need to open the peerScholar assignment from your Canvas course\.

1.  Log in to your Canvas course and find your peerScholar assignment\.
2.  Click the **peerScholar assignment** you want to open\. If prompted, click **Load \[assignment name\] in a new window**\. To ensure the assignment opens properly, please allow pop\-up windows in your browser\.
3.  You will see an overview of the activities assigned to your course\. Click one of the phases \(**Create**, **Assess**, or **Reflect**\) to complete that part of the assignment\.
4.  Read the instructions for each phase carefully, taking note of the objectives and prompts\. Most instructors will provide a customized rubric to guide you in completing each part of the peer assessment process\. Click **Let's Go\!** to proceed\.
5.  To complete the phase, you may be instructed to type up a response, attach a file, or carry out a task\.
6.  Once you are satisfied with your response, click **Submit** or **Save and Submit**\.
    -   If you are not ready to submit, click **Save as Draft**\. You can continue to work on your response while the phase is still open; it will be marked as "Complete" only after you submit your response\.
7.  You can resubmit work until the due date passes or the instructor manually closes the phase\. Once the phase closes, your submission will be locked and you can no longer resubmit for that phase\.

#### Tips

-   **The contextual commenting \(annotating\) feature in the "Assess" phase varies depending on the file type submitted**\. To annotate a peer's text submission, select the text you would like to comment on and click the pencil icon that appears above the highlighted text\. Click "Save" after writing your comment\. Please note that you cannot directly annotate on an attached file\.

[> Troubleshoot issues with submitting peerScholar work](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/peerscholar-student-guide/#troubleshoot-issues)

### Troubleshoot issues with submitting peerScholar work

If something goes wrong while you are trying to submit your assignment, you can try to resolve certain issues yourself\. Your instructor will also be able to check your progress throughout the assignment and confirm your submission\.

#### General troubleshooting tips

1.  Ensure that you have a stable internet connection\.
2.  Switch to a computer if you are submitting from a mobile device\.
3.  Update your web browser to the latest version or try a different browser\. We recommend using Chrome or Firefox for the most reliable experience\.
4.  Disable any extensions/add\-ons in your web browser\.
5.  Disable any VPN \(Virtual Private Network\)\.
6.  Restart your device and try to submit your assignment again\.

#### Unable to complete a phase

The assignment schedule set by your instructor will affect when you can complete each phase of the assignment\. First, check the status of the phase\.

-   Is the phase still open? You can only complete a phase when it is green, has an upcoming due date, and/or its status is "In Progress"\.
-   If you would like to complete a phase but its status is now "Closed" or the submission deadline has passed, please contact your instructor or teaching assistant for your next steps\.

[> Review your graded work in peerScholar](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/peerscholar-student-guide/#review-graded-work)

### Review your graded work in peerScholar

Not all instructors will release grades using peerScholar; please reach out directly if you are not sure what to expect in your course\.

1.  Log in to your Canvas course and find your peerScholar assignment\.
2.  Click the **peerScholar assignment** you want to review\. If prompted, click **Load \[assignment name\] in a new window**\. To ensure the assignment opens properly, please allow pop\-up windows in your browser\.
3.  On the left sidebar in peerScholar, click **Marks & Review**\.
    -   You will be able to see the grades you received for each activity\. Grades will be listed as "Not Available" if your instructor has not yet released the grades\.
4.  Click **Review** to see your original submission, your grade for each phase of the activity, and your instructor's or teaching assistant's feedback\.

## peerScholar FAQ

Find UBC\-specific answers to frequently asked questions by clicking any accordion bar below\.

[> My instructor said that everyone would receive a certain number of reviews from peers, so why did I receive fewer?](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/peerscholar-student-guide/#amount-of-review)

You may receive fewer reviews than the instructor set if students assigned to your work do not complete their reviews\.

[> Can I choose which assignments I get to review?](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/peerscholar-student-guide/#choice-of-reviews)

No, the assignments you receive to review are distributed randomly by peerScholar\.

[> Can I choose which group I'm in for group work activities?](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/peerscholar-student-guide/#choice-of-group)

Instructors may set up the peerScholar groups randomly, manually, or by letting the students choose\. If students are allowed to choose their groups, you will be able to select the group you would like to work in\. Otherwise, it will be chosen by your instructor or by peerScholar\.

[> What is the maximum file size I can upload to peerScholar?](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/peerscholar-student-guide/#maximum-upload-size)

The maximum file size is 500MB\.

## Where can I get more support with peerScholar?

### Technical support

**If you have trouble accessing peerScholar:**

-   Contact us for assistance:  
    604 827 4775 or [LT\.hub@ubc\.ca](mailto:LT.hub@ubc.ca) or visit the [LT Hub online](https://lthub.ubc.ca/dropin)\.

**If you experience technical issues while using peerScholar:**

-   Submit a request to the [peerScholar Support Center](https://support.peerscholar.com/hc/en-us/requests/new)\.
-   Reach out to your instructors or teaching assistants for time\-sensitive questions, as they can provide real\-time assistance in helping you resolve issues\.

---

### Online learning support

-   Visit UBC’s [Keep Learning site](http://keeplearning.ubc.ca/) and the Chapman Learning Common’s [student toolkits](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/category/type/interactive/)\.
-   Visit the [UBC Vancouver’s Centre for Accessibility page](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility) or the [UBC Okanagan’s Disability Resource Centre page](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/academic-success/disability-resources/) to learn more about available support for students with disabilities and ongoing medical conditions\.

#### Learn more

-   For more information on peerScholar, including video demos and research, explore [peerScholar’s videos website](https://videos.peerscholar.com/)\.

---

title: iClicker Cloud Student Guide
content_markdown:
[iClicker Cloud logo](https://lthub.ubc.ca/2020/07/iClicker-Cloud-Logo-150x150.png)

**iClicker Cloud is an online student response system that allows you to respond to polls and quizzes during a class session, using your computer or mobile device**\. When you answer questions, your instructor receives your responses instantly and may share the results and the correct answers during the class session or afterward\.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Access** | *Immediate* | You can [set up an iClicker student account](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/iclicker-cloud-student-guide/#set-up-account), then use the same account to [log in to iClicker](https://student.iclicker.com/#/login)\. |
| **Bandwidth** | *Yes* | Low demand on internet connections\. |
| **Privacy** | *Yes* | Complies with UBC’s privacy requirements\. |

### What will I use it for?

Your instructor may have you use iClicker Cloud for a variety of activities:

-   Test your understanding or share your opinions at different points during a class session
-   Participate in peer instruction, where you answer a question, discuss it in small groups, and answer again
-   Record your attendance at a class session
-   Study outside of class sessions

This tool guide was last reviewed in November 2025 with version 7\.2\.0 of iClicker Cloud\.

## What do I need to use iClicker Cloud?

### A supported web browser

iClicker runs in your web browser and supports Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari\. You may find it more convenient to use the iClicker Student application that is available on mobile devices, especially if you are using your computer for other course activities\. For more information regarding compatible versions, please refer to the [iClicker Student app requirements](https://mhe.my.site.com/iclicker/s/article/What-are-the-system-requirements-for-using-the-iClicker-student-app)\.

---

### A UBC iClicker Cloud student account

You will need to create an iClicker account that is associated with UBC, as outlined in the accordion section below\.

#### Tips

-   **The student version of iClicker Cloud is called iClicker Student on both the website and the mobile app**\. These two terms are interchangeable, and you may see your instructor use either one\.
-   **If you encounter issues connecting to iClicker, you can try to troubleshoot them yourself using the [iClicker troubleshooting tips](https://mhe.my.site.com/iclicker/s/article/How-to-Troubleshoot-Your-Connection-to-the-iClicker-Student-App)\.** You can also reach out to your instructor or teaching assistants, as they may be able to provide real\-time assistance in helping you resolve issues\. If the iClicker issues are still not resolved, you may [contact us](https://lthub.ubc.ca/support/lt-hub/#contact-info) at the LT Hub\.

## How do I use iClicker Cloud?

You will need to set up an iClicker account to get started\. After setting up your account, you can join a live class session and participate in the iClicker activities that your instructor facilitates during lectures\.

Click any accordion bar below to find instructions and tips for setting up and participating with iClicker Cloud\.

Expand All

[> Set up an iClicker Cloud account](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/iclicker-cloud-student-guide/#set-up-account)

### Set up an iClicker Cloud account

Note that if you have already made an iClicker Cloud account for another course, you can use that same account to log in and [manually add another iClicker course to your account](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/iclicker-cloud-student-guide/#add-course)\.

1.  If you have not already made an iClicker account for another course, go to the [iClicker Student account creation page](https://app.reef-education.com/#/account/create)\.
2.  Type "University of British Columbia" into the "Find Your Institution" field, choose **University of British Columbia** from the search results, and click **Next**\.
3.  Enter the rest of your information\.
    -   For iClicker and Canvas to sync, your iClicker account email must match your default email in your Canvas account\. You can check and change which email you have listed as default in Canvas by following the [instructions under “Tips” section of the “Manage Canvas notifications” accordion](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/canvas-student-guide/#manage-notifications)\.
    -   Make sure to enter your UBC student number into the "Student ID" field\. This number will link your Canvas account to your iClicker account, so please enter it accurately and only use it for one iClicker account\.
4.  Once you are ready, agree to the **Privacy Notice / Terms of Use** and the **treatment of personal information**, then click **Create Account**\.
    -   If you are not comfortable agreeing to these items with your regular email address, you can set up an anonymized email address to use instead\. Please note that your instructor may see this email address in the iClicker activity reports\.
5.  You now have an account and are ready to add a course following the instructions in the accordion directly below\.

#### Tips

-   **You only need to complete these steps once**\. After you have created your UBC iClicker account the first time, you should use the same account to access any subsequent UBC courses that have iClicker activities\.

[> Add an iClicker Cloud course to your account](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/iclicker-cloud-student-guide/#add-course)

### Add an iClicker Cloud course to your account

Most instructors will sync iClicker with Canvas\. As long as you have added your UBC student number to your iClicker account, you will automatically be enrolled in your course\(s\) with no extra steps needed\.

However, if you do not see your course in iClicker, your instructor may have set up your iClicker course to allow students to self\-enroll\. In this case, you can enroll yourself manually:

1.  [Log in to iClicker](https://student.iclicker.com/) using your iClicker account email and password\.
2.  Click the **plus sign** in the top\-right corner of the screen, choose **University of British Columbia** from the available options, and type in the name of the iClicker course that your instructor has provided\.
3.  Click the **course** you would like to join, and click **Add this course**\.
4.  You will now see and be able to access this course on your Courses page\.

[> Join a class session in iClicker Cloud](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/iclicker-cloud-student-guide/#join-class-session)

### Join a class session in iClicker Cloud

After you add a course to your account, you will join that course in iClicker each time there is a class session to attend\.

1.  [Log in to iClicker](https://student.iclicker.com/#/login) using your iClicker account email and password\.
    -   If you do not have an account, follow the [steps to set up an iClicker account](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/iclicker-cloud-student-guide/#set-up-account)\.
2.  Click the **course name**\.
3.  Click **Join** when it appears on your screen \(it may take a minute to show up\)\. Note that this button only displays once your instructor has manually started the class on their instructor iClicker account\. The option to join the course will not be available if you log in early\.
4.  You will see a confirmation message, and your instructor will see from their iClicker instructor account that you have joined the class\.

#### Tips

-   **Joining a class session enables you to participate in the iClicker activities during class\.** These activities include answering polls or quizzes\.
-   **The time when you join a class session is recorded and visible to your instructor\.** To ensure you receive full participation credit, it is best to join on time\.
-   **Not all instructors track attendance with iClicker Cloud\.** You can ask your instructor if you are not sure\.

[> Participate in iClicker Cloud activities](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/iclicker-cloud-student-guide/#participate-in-activities)

### Participate in iClicker Cloud activities

When your instructor initiates an iClicker activity during the class session, you will see the options for responding to it in the iClicker interface\.

-   For polls, you may see a screenshot of the question to answer alongside the response options\.
-   For quizzes, you will only see the response options\.
-   For both activity types, your instructor will share the questions with you in the live class, though the format will vary based on whether your class is in person, online, or hybrid\.

Please note that some instructors may choose to show questions only for those students in attendance, so you may have to be present in class in real time \(whether it is in person or online\) to see the questions\. Instructors may also limit attendance\-taking only to those students whose devices are in the physical classroom\. You can ask if you are not sure whether these features will be used\.

1.  Once you have [logged in to iClicker](https://student.iclicker.com/#/login) and joined the class session, wait for your instructor to initiate an activity\.
2.  When an activity starts, you will see a question number and your options for responding on your screen:
    -   For [polls](https://mhe.my.site.com/iclicker/s/article/How-to-Participate-in-a-Poll-with-the-iClicker-Student-App), you may be able to see a screenshot of the question to answer\. You will respond to a single question in one of several ways, depending on how your instructor has set it up: by choosing one or more multiple\-choice items, writing a short answer \(up to 140 characters\), typing a numeric or formula\-based answer, or clicking part of an image\.
    -   For [quizzes](https://mhe.my.site.com/iclicker/s/article/How-to-Participate-in-a-Quiz-with-the-iClicker-Student-App), you will answer a set of questions by choosing a multiple\-choice item for each, then reviewing and submitting all your answers together\.
3.  Follow the prompts on screen to submit each answer\. When completing a poll, you will see an “Answer Received” for each question\. For a quiz, you will see a "Quiz Submitted" once you have finished the set of questions and submitted your entire response\.
4.  When an activity ends, your instructor may choose to share the correct poll response and/or class results\. Quiz results may also be available after the class session ends\. Viewing the iClicker poll and/or quiz results is dependent on whether or not your instructor chooses to share the results\. Check with your instructor if you are not sure\.

#### Tips

-   **You may change your answer as many times as you like, up until the point your instructor closes the answering period**\. Instructors cannot re\-open polls or quizzes, so make sure to review your answers before submitting your responses\.
-   **If you see an anonymous icon for a question, your answer will not be tied to your identity**\. However, your response to an anonymous question may still count for participation points\.
-   **Re\-join the session if you accidentally close or get bumped out of iClicker during a lecture \(e\.g\., you lose your internet connection\)**\. If you miss any iClicker activities during a class session, let your instructor know, as they may be willing to adjust your participation for that session\.
-   **You can review iClicker polls outside of class to help you study, as every question asked is recorded as part of the course**\. Click the “Class History” tab when you first log in, and read about the available [iClicker features that can help you study](https://mhe.my.site.com/iclicker/s/article/How-to-Use-iClicker-s-Student-Study-Tools)\.
-   **Make sure your iClicker work honestly reflects your learning and not anybody else's**\. Letting someone else answer your questions with your iClicker account counts as [academic misconduct](https://academicintegrity.ubc.ca/regulation-process/academic-misconduct/)\.

## iClicker Cloud FAQ

Find UBC\-specific answers to frequently asked questions by clicking any accordion bar below\.

[> What can I do if I cannot see my course in iClicker?](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/iclicker-cloud-student-guide/#course-access)

If you do not see the course in your list of courses, try to [manually add an iClicker course to your account](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/iclicker-cloud-student-guide/#add-course)\.

If you still cannot see your course:

1.  Make sure your UBC student number has been added correctly to your iClicker account\.
    -   To verify, [log in to iClicker](https://student.iclicker.com/#/login), click the **three lines** at the top\-left corner, and select **Profile**\.
    -   Ensure that you entered your UBC student number—not your UBC CWL—in the "Student ID" field\.
2.  If you have added your UBC student number to your iClicker account correctly, it is possible that you have multiple iClicker accounts with the same student number\. iClicker will not add duplicate student numbers to the same iClicker course\.
    -   If you think this might be the case, [log in to iClicker](https://student.iclicker.com/#/login) using your duplicate account\(s\) and remove your UBC student number from the “Student ID” field\. Please ensure that your student number remains linked to the account you wish to continue using\.
    -   Log in to the iClicker account you wish to continue using\. Your courses should now appear under Courses\.
    -   If you still do not see your courses, please contact your instructor and have them re\-sync the course roster\.
3.  Make sure that your default email in Canvas matches the email that you used to make an iClicker account\. This matching will ensure that the right iClicker account is added to your iClicker course\.
    -   You can check and change which email you have listed in Canvas by following the [instructions under “Tips” section of the “Manage Canvas notifications” accordion](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/canvas-student-guide/#manage-notifications)\.
4.  If you are still experiencing issues with seeing your course, please [contact us](https://lthub.ubc.ca/support/lt-hub/#contact-info) at the LT Hub for further assistance\.

[> What can I do if I cannot see my iClicker grades in Canvas?](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/iclicker-cloud-student-guide/#grade-access)

If you have properly linked your iClicker account with Canvas \(i\.e\., by ensuring both your iClicker and Canvas emails match and your UBC student number is correctly entered in “Student ID”\), and you cannot see your grades in Canvas, it is possible that your instructor has not set up iClicker to sync grades with Canvas\. Not all instructors plan to release iClicker grades in Canvas\. Please ask your instructor or teaching assistants if you are not sure\.

If your instructor has set up grade syncing between iClicker and Canvas and you are still having trouble seeing your grades, please [contact us](https://lthub.ubc.ca/support/lt-hub/#contact-info) at the LT Hub for assistance\.

[> What can I do if I have trouble connecting during a class session?](https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/iclicker-cloud-student-guide/#connection-issues)

You can try to troubleshoot some connection issues yourself using the [iClicker troubleshooting tips](https://mhe.my.site.com/iclicker/s/article/How-to-Troubleshoot-Your-Connection-to-the-iClicker-Student-App)\.

You can also reach out to your instructors or teaching assistants, as they may be able to provide real\-time assistance in helping you resolve issues\. If not, they will at least know that you were trying to participate but could not connect during the class session\.

## Where can I get more support with iClicker Cloud?

### Technical support

**If you have trouble with iClicker:**

-   Contact the [UBC IT Service Centre Help Desk](https://it.ubc.ca/got-question-about-it-products-and-support#helpdesk):  
    604 822 2008 or fill out the [UBC IT request form](https://ubc.service-now.com/selfservice?id=sc_cat_item_v2&sys_id=cc7f5fb9874e0100bbee70406d434df9)\.
-   Contact iClicker support directly for further assistance:  
    Fill out the [iClicker support web form](https://mhe.my.site.com/iclicker/s/contactsupport)\.
-   For time\-sensitive questions, reach out to your instructors or teaching assistants, as they may be able to provide real\-time assistance in helping you resolve issues\.

### Online learning support

-   Visit UBC’s [Keep Learning site](http://keeplearning.ubc.ca/) and the Chapman Learning Common’s [student toolkits](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/category/type/interactive/)\.
-   Visit the [UBC Vancouver’s Centre for Accessibility page](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility) or the [UBC Okanagan’s Disability Resource Centre page](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/academic-success/disability-resources/) to learn more about available support for students with disabilities and ongoing medical conditions\.
